citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not communicate timely, updated information about the health and well-being of two adult goats to the
attending veterinarian.
A VMO observed two adult goats (“Trixie” and “Gypsy”) with a significant limp. The VMO observed Trixie reluctant to bear
weight on her left front leg with slow, stiff, movement in her rear back legs. She was also seen kneeling on her front legs,
reluctant to walk, and slow to sit down and get up. Gypsy was observed with a significant limp on her right front leg when
walking, and holding up that leg when standing. She was slow to stand from a resting position. Both goats demonstrated
abnormal behavior on the affected front leg: a repetitive kicking motion.
The licensee initiated NSAID pain medication according to veterinary guidance: Trixie, several months prior, and Gypsy,
about 2 months prior to the inspection. The facility observed some improvement with Trixie's mobility and noticed that on
some occasions, Trixie appears energetic, and other times, Trixie is not weight bearing. However, the licensee and
attending veterinarian confirmed that the licensee has not updated the attending veterinarian about the condition of the
two animals since Gypsy was prescribed the medication. The attending veterinarian stated that in prior conversations, he
informed the licensee to update him if the animals' condition did not substantially improve.
Failing to communicate timely and accurate information on these animals' health, behavior, and well-being is preventing
the attending veterinarian from using appropriate methods to control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries.
Correct by ensuring these two animals are evaluated by a licensed veterinarian and ensuring a mechanism of direct and
frequent communication to the attending veterinarian so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal
health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed.
Correction date: 10/31/2026.

The facility is not storing food for its 12 goats and 2 pigs in facilities that adequately protect the food.
The inspector observed two facilities that store food. The first facility, the "sunroom" contained food stored in bags on the
floor. This facility, which previously housed birds, contained an accumulation of various dusty items, debris, feathers, and
bird stool. An excessive number of flies were present. Four bins of food were stored on a porch that has only a roof. Free
roaming birds have access to the porch storing these receptacles. Some flies were visible within one of the receptacles.
Improper storage of food can lead to contamination or molding from animals, vermin, or moisture. This can lead to
disease or deterioration of the food.
Correct by ensuring that supplies of food and bedding are stored in facilities that adequately protect such supplies against
deterioration, molding, or contamination by vermin.
Correction date: December 1, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
